title: uPVC Column Pipe Classes Explained: Class 1, 2, 3 and 4
metaTitle: uPVC Column Pipe Classes 1, 2, 3 & 4 Explained | Prayag
description: Understand uPVC column pipe Classes 1, 2, 3 and 4 and how borewell depth, pressure and pump load influence the right selection.
bodyHtml:
A borewell column pipe does more than carry water. It operates vertically, forms part of a suspended assembly and has to cope with the pressure and mechanical demands created by the pump, water column and installation depth.

That is why uPVC column pipe classes matter. Prayag offers lead-free uPVC Column Pipes from Class 1 through Class 4 for different borewell operating conditions. Understanding the purpose of these classes helps pump dealers, installers, farmers and property owners avoid selecting a pipe only by diameter.

What Is a uPVC Column Pipe?

A column pipe acts as the rising main in a borewell. The submersible pump sits below the water level and pushes water upward through the pipe to the surface.

Unlike an ordinary horizontal water line, the column also forms part of a suspended vertical installation. The pipe and its threaded joints therefore need to handle hydraulic pressure and mechanical load together.

Why Are Column Pipes Divided Into Classes?

Different borewells operate under different conditions. A shallow domestic installation and a deep agricultural borewell may use different pumps, experience different head and create different suspended loads.

The class system provides pipe options for these varying duties. Prayag categorises its range from Class 1 for standard conditions through Class 4 for more demanding applications.

Class 1 uPVC Column Pipes

Prayag positions Class 1 for standard borewell applications and moderate operating conditions. It is intended for installations where pressure and load requirements fall within the corresponding duty range.

“Standard” should not be interpreted as one fixed depth suitable everywhere. Pump head, total load, water level and pipe diameter still need to be considered.

Class 2 uPVC Column Pipes

Class 2 is intended for conditions requiring greater pressure and mechanical capability than Class 1. Prayag positions it for medium-depth applications.

This illustrates why diameter alone is not enough. Two pipes with the same diameter can be intended for different operating loads depending on their class.

Class 3 uPVC Column Pipes

Class 3 moves into more demanding borewell conditions. Prayag recommends this category for deeper installations where greater load-bearing strength is required.

At increased depth, the suspended pipe length and hydraulic head can become more significant. Joint strength, tensile performance and pressure capability therefore need to work together.

Class 4 uPVC Column Pipes

Class 4 is the extra-heavy-duty category in Prayag's current range. It is intended for demanding borewell installations and challenging operating conditions.

It should not automatically be selected simply because it is the highest class. The correct class is the one that matches the actual pump, depth and load requirements.

Column Pipe Class and Borewell Depth

Depth is one of the most visible selection factors, but it should not be used alone. A deeper installation generally means more suspended pipe and can also involve greater pumping head.

However, two borewells of similar total depth may have different static water levels, pumping water levels and pump duties. Final selection should therefore consider the complete operating system.

Pump Capacity Matters

The submersible pump creates pressure inside the column pipe. Different pumps have different head and discharge characteristics.

Installing a high-head pump on a pipe selected only for diameter can create an unsuitable combination. Pump model, operating point and discharge requirement should be known before the final class is chosen.

Static and Dynamic Water Levels

Borewell depth is not the same as pumping head. Static water level is the level before pumping, while the pumping level can fall when the system is operating.

That drawdown changes the lifting requirement. Accurate specification therefore needs more than the total drilled depth. Water-level data and delivery elevation help define the actual system head.

Column Pipe Diameter Is a Separate Decision

Prayag's current uPVC Column Pipe range spans nominal sizes from 1 inch to 4 inches depending on class and type. Diameter should suit flow and pump connection requirements.

Class relates to the pressure and mechanical duty. Choosing the diameter does not automatically choose the class, and choosing a class does not automatically determine the diameter.

Why Joint Strength Matters

Every threaded connection forms part of the vertical assembly. If a joint fails deep inside a borewell, the consequences can be much more serious than a small leak in accessible plumbing.

Prayag uses precision-engineered threaded joints and emphasises leak resistance and load-bearing capability. Correct tightening and alignment remain essential during installation.

Coupler Type vs Belling Type

Prayag offers both Coupler Type and Belling Type Column Pipes. Coupler Type uses a separate threaded coupler and is positioned for enhanced joint strength and higher-load or deeper applications.

Belling Type incorporates the connection into the pipe end, reducing separate components and supporting faster installation in standard and medium-depth applications. The correct system should match the borewell duty.

Why Corrosion Resistance Helps

Metal column pipes can be exposed continuously to water and underground conditions. uPVC does not rust in the same way as metal, which can reduce one source of long-term deterioration.

Prayag highlights corrosion-free performance as a benefit of its lead-free uPVC Column Pipe system. Water chemistry and complete system design should still be considered when planning the borewell installation.

Agricultural Applications

Agricultural borewells often operate for long periods and may need to deliver substantial water volumes. Correct pipe selection helps ensure that the rising main matches the pump and the depth.

Farmers should avoid replacing a failed pipe by simply buying the same diameter without checking whether the previous class was suitable. Pump duty and borewell conditions should be reviewed first.

Domestic and Commercial Borewells

Homes, residential societies and commercial properties may use borewell water for storage or distribution. The pumping system can include a column pipe, delivery line, storage tank and automatic controls.

The complete route from pump to storage should therefore be considered. Tank elevation, required discharge and the pump's operating head all influence the column-pipe duty.

Why Choose Prayag uPVC Column Pipes?

Prayag's uPVC Column Pipe range uses lead-free uPVC and is available from Class 1 through Class 4. Sizes extend from 1 inch to 4 inches depending on the class and configuration, and users can choose between Coupler Type and Belling Type systems.

Prayag highlights precision-thread manufacturing, load-bearing strength, corrosion resistance, lightweight handling and long-term reliability. The range is intended for domestic, agricultural, commercial and industrial borewell applications.

Conclusion

Class 1, Class 2, Class 3 and Class 4 are not simply four price levels. They exist because borewell operating conditions vary.

The right uPVC column pipe should match borewell depth, pump head, discharge, suspended load, pipe diameter and joint requirements. Selecting the appropriate class from the beginning can make the complete pumping system more dependable.

Practical Borewell Selection Checklist

Before choosing a column pipe class, collect a complete set of borewell and pump information. Record total bore depth, static water level, expected pumping water level, pump installation depth, pump model, pump head, required discharge, delivery elevation and nominal connection size. These inputs give the installer a much clearer picture than borewell depth or motor horsepower alone.

Next, confirm the required pipe diameter from the hydraulic duty and the class from the pressure and suspended-load requirements. Check whether Coupler Type or Belling Type is more appropriate for the installation. Inspect the pipe threads and connections before lowering the assembly, and ensure the lifting arrangement can handle the complete suspended system safely. If the pump is later replaced with a different head or discharge model, the column-pipe specification should be reviewed again rather than assuming the existing class will automatically remain suitable.

It is also useful to document the final pipe class, size, connection type and number of lengths after installation. Borewell components are largely hidden once commissioned, so an accurate service record can save time during future pump maintenance. A simple installation sheet kept with the pump model and borewell data gives future technicians a reliable reference instead of forcing them to estimate what is below ground.

For best results, the final selection should also be checked against the pump manufacturer guidance and the borewell contractor’s installation method. This additional coordination helps ensure that pipe class, thread type, diameter and pump duty are treated as one system rather than separate purchase decisions.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many uPVC Column Pipe classes does Prayag offer?

Prayag currently offers Class 1, Class 2, Class 3 and Class 4.

Is Class 4 always the best column pipe?

No. Class 4 is intended for demanding conditions. The correct class should match actual borewell and pump requirements.

What sizes are Prayag Column Pipes available in?

The current range spans approximately 1 inch to 4 inches depending on type and class.

Are Prayag Column Pipes lead-free?

Prayag states that its uPVC Column Pipes are manufactured using lead-free uPVC compounds.
